readings:
Lower brickwork

15 GAR ÚS · 15 GAR SAG · 5½ GAR SUKUD

Length 15 rods; breadth 15 rods; height 5½ rods: the lower brickwork.

Numerical reading aid from Scheil's p. 300, with normalized sign labels. At the chosen 6 m conversion: 90 × 90 × 33 m. The retained BTTo transliteration displays 2½ here while its translation reads 5½; this activity explicitly follows the 5½ in the retained 1914 numerical row and the conventional scheme.

Second storey

13 GAR ÚS · 13 GAR SAG · 3 GAR SUKUD · rik-bi 2-ú

Length 13 rods; breadth 13 rods; height 3 rods: the second storey.

A normalized numerical aid, not a diplomatic transcription. The photograph's second terrace is much shallower when the stone's image is projected with one uniform scale.

Third storey

10 GAR ÚS · 10 GAR SAG · 1 GAR SUKUD · U₅ 3-šú

Length 10 rods; breadth 10 rods; height 1 rod: the third storey.

A normalized aid to the numerical row. At 6 m per rod this is 60 × 60 × 6 m. The 6 m height belongs to this conventional reading; it is not a new measurement of a surviving terrace.

Fourth storey

8½ GAR ÚS · 8½ GAR SAG · 1 GAR SUKUD · U₅ 4-ú

Length 8½ rods; breadth 8½ rods; height 1 rod: the fourth storey.

The half rod changes the footprint to 51 × 51 m under this conversion. The row gives dimensions, while the centred position in the comparison drawing remains a modern convention.

Fifth, then seventh

7 GAR ÚS · 7 GAR SAG · 1 GAR SUKUD · U₅ 5-šú … U₅ 7-ú

The fifth storey is given dimensions. The next surviving row names the seventh. There is no written sixth-storey dimension row in between.

The ellipsis is this lesson's omission marker. Modern editors supply a sixth row. Use the missing-level controls to distinguish a supplied value from a written one.

Top sanctuary

4 GAR ÚS · 3¾ GAR SAG · 2½ GAR SUKUD

Length 4 rods; breadth 3¾ rods; height 2½ rods: the upper sanctuary.

The breadth follows the modern 3¾ interpretation. Scheil's 1914 page reads the fractional expression differently. At 6 m per rod, the scheme is 24 × 22.5 × 15 m; it is not a 24 m square.

Copied and checked

GABA.RI bar-sip.KI … SAR-ma … ù ba-ri

A duplicate from Borsippa … written … and checked.

words:
ÚS · šiddu

length. A sign label in capitals, followed by the Akkadian word. Scheil writes uš; the modern corpus lemmatizes the word as šiddu. Do not pronounce the capital sign label as an Akkadian sentence.

SAG · pūtu

breadth. Literally also 'front' or 'forehead'. In these measurements it names the breadth. A second horizontal dimension does not tell us where the next terrace sits.

SUKUD · mēlû

height. Scheil uses gud in his older transliteration. The modern sign label SUKUD is associated with Akkadian mēlû. The units still have to be identified before converting to metres.

GAR / NINDA · nindanu

a measuring rod; a length unit. The numerical comparison uses the conventional conversion 1 nindanu = 12 ordinary cubits ≈ 6 m. The tablet also discusses other cubit standards: a single automatic conversion is not valid for its entire text.

KÙŠ · ammatu

cubit. A length unit, not one universal modern length. The 90 m tablet-derived scheme and a 91.5 m excavated base are kept separate rather than silently equated.

rik-bi / U₅ · rikbu

storey. The second storey is written with a syllabic word; later rows use a sign. The label seventh after fifth is evidence for a gap, not surviving measurements for the gap.

KI.TA · šaplû

lower. The lower brickwork in the first numerical row. It does not by itself tell us the construction date, material strengths or present surviving height.

AN.TA · elû

upper. The upper sanctum belongs above the terraces. Its 4 by 3¾ nindanu footprint is rectangular; the drawing below shows a front elevation, not a square plan.
